earlier_scan.source_named: Adelaar, K. Alexander. 2005. Salako or Badamea: Sketch grammar, texts and lexicon of the Kendayan dialect of West Borneo. Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz.

new_statements.quote: Salako has eight vowel phonemes: i, e, ə, a, o, ɔ, u and ʉ. There are no diphthongs, except in loan words such as the Malay function words kalaw 'if, when' and ataw 'or' (usually pronounced kalo and ato respectively). Stress is non-phonemic and falls on the last syllable.
new_statements.citation: Adelaar, K. Alexander. 2002. Salako morphology and the interrelation between voice, mood and aspect. In K. new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Salako is not contrastive and falls predictably on the final syllable of the word. Corroborated in the same chapter by fn. 4 (p. 1), which transcribes the ethnonym Kendayan as [kanay'otn] / [kanay'ɔtn] with the stress mark before the last syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. (Fn. 13, p. 4, notes that words of more than two syllables, including loans, often show a schwa or reduced first syllable, i.e. non-final syllables are the reduced ones, consistent with final prominence.) Note the conflicting 1949 remark by Dunselman for the Mempawah-hinterland (Ahe-area) Kendayan dialect, 'een duidelijk accent op de paenultima' (penultimate) -- a different dialect and an impressionistic missionary note.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; stated in a brief phonemic sketch (the author defers to Adelaar 1991 'A phonological sketch of Salako' for detail). Language = Salako/bahasa Damea of Sambas regency (W. Kalimantan) and Lundu (Sarawak); main informant Vitus Kaslem of Nyarumkop; field data 1986-1990.
new_statements.identity_note: sela1262 is a Glottolog bookkeeping code: ISO [skl] 'Selako' was merged into [knx] Kendayan by CR 2007-261 (effective 2008-01-14), so the living entry is kend1254 Kendayan (Kanayatn). Selako = Salako = bahasa (Ba)Damea, the Kanayatn dialect of Sambas regency (West Kalimantan) and Lundu district (Sarawak). The statement quoted is about exactly this Salako variety (Adelaar's informant from Nyarumkop, Sambas), so it fits sela1262 precisely; the same file and statement are already held under kend1254, where the earlier audit also holds Dunselman 1949's conflicting penultimate-accent remark for the Ahe-area Kendayan dialect. If the catalog collapses bookkeeping codes into their successor, this entry should be merged with kend1254 rather than counted separately.

sources.note: Sec. 2 'Explanatory notes on Salako phonemics and morphophonemics', p. 2: 'Stress is non-phonemic and falls on the last syllable.' Fn. 4 p. 1 gives Kendayan pronounced [kanay'otn] with the stress mark before the final syllable. Variety = Salako (bahasa Damea) of Sambas regency and Lundu (Sarawak), i.e. exactly the variety the retired [skl] code denoted; informant Vitus Kaslem of Nyarumkop; refers to Adelaar 1991 for the full phonology.

sources.note: Inleiding p. 61: 'heeft daarbij een duidelijk accent op de paenultima' (clear penultimate accent) -- but for the Mempawah-hinterland (Ahe-area) Kendayan, not Salako; a missionary's impressionistic remark that conflicts with Adelaar's final-stress statement for Salako.
Retired entry: 'Merge into Kendayan; Salako [knx]', CR 2007-261; no descriptive references attached; descriptive literature sits under kend1254.
No phonology; confirms Selako/Salako = Kendayan of Sarawak/Sambas, cites Adelaar 2005 (Harrassowitz) and Thomas et al. 1985.
